subject: statin
correct: On a statin (NHS England statin intolerance pathway): CK <4× ULN with tolerable symptoms → continue/review; CK 4–10× ULN or intolerable symptoms → stop for 4–6 weeks, then rechallenge (lower dose/different statin) once resolved; CK >10× ULN → stop, urgent assessment (check renal function). NICE NG238's 5× ULN rule applies only BEFORE starting. The site's lab guides, angina, tia-stroke and management/hypercholesterolaemia already use 4–10× / 4–6 weeks.

fixes.old: CK 5-10× ULN: stop statin; confirm resolution; rechallenge with different statin after 4 weeks; monitor CK
fixes.new: CK 4–10× ULN or intolerable symptoms: stop statin for 4–6 weeks; confirm resolution; then rechallenge at a lower dose or with a different statin; monitor CK (NHS England statin intolerance pathway)

fixes.old: Myopathy (CK >5× ULN): 1-3 per 100,000 patient-years; stop statin; usually resolves.

subject: CRP
correct: GCA: CRP/ESR are usually raised (often markedly) but there is no >200 mg/L criterion; a normal or moderately raised CRP does not exclude GCA (BSR 2020).

subject: CRP
correct: Truelove & Witts acute severe UC: ≥6 bloody stools/day plus ≥1 of HR >90, temp >37.8 °C, Hb <105 g/L, ESR >30 mm/h (CRP >30 mg/L in modified versions). CRP >45 mg/L is the Oxford DAY-3 IV-steroid rescue criterion, not a severity criterion combined with Hb.

fixes.old: Hb <105 g/L with CRP >45 mg/L indicates severe disease.
fixes.new: Hb <105 g/L (with ≥6 bloody stools a day) is a Truelove and Witts severe criterion; CRP >45 mg/L matters on day 3 of IV steroids (Oxford rescue criterion).

fixes.old: Hb <105 g/L with CRP >45 mg/L indicates severe disease.
fixes.new: Hb <105 g/L (with ≥6 bloody stools a day) is a Truelove and Witts severe criterion; CRP >45 mg/L matters on day 3 of IV steroids (Oxford rescue criterion).

note: The same page's own Truelove and Witts box (line ~82) is correct; this sentence conflates two scores.
